source.title: Improving Sharpness-Aware Minimization with Fisher Mask for Better Generalization on Language Models
source.authors: Qi-Huang Zhong; Liang Ding; Li Shen; Peng Mi; Ju-Hua Liu; Bo Du; Da-Cheng Tao

record.file_problem: none; supplied text includes the paper and appendix
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether sharpness-related measurements track generalization, using language-model fine-tuning and loss-landscape visualizations rather than the claim versions’ original methods.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates SAM and FSAM on downstream development-set scores, including comparisons of optimizer performance. These scores do not report the training-versus-test error gap required by V4, and the paper does not test the other versions. Loss landscape figures and performance scores are not direct measures of V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization premise to develop FSAM and evaluates its downstream performance. It does not test any stated version: its landscape visualizations do not measure V7's perturbation tolerance against training–test gaps, and its optimizer comparisons lack an SGD or momentum-SGD baseline for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the authors' overall conclusion: FSAM improves SAM's performance and language-model generalization across their evaluated settings. Their assertion of consistent improvement should be read at the aggregate level; individual task metrics include ties and regressions. Computational savings remain potential because actual sparse acceleration was not implemented.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes pretrained language models with Adam, SAM, or the proposed Fisher-masked SAM; evaluates downstream development metrics, not the claim versions’ specified interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: FSAM performance varies with sparse ratio and Fisher-mask update interval; the authors report the best performance at sparse ratio 0.9 and caution that too-small update intervals may affect optimization stability.

fits_no_version.finding: FSAM improves average development scores over SAM across the four large language-understanding models by 0.67–1.98 points, with additional generation and transfer-task improvements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher-masked SAM can improve downstream performance over vanilla SAM when fine-tuning pretrained language models.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6.4 reports flatter FSAM landscapes using filter-normalized random directions and interpolation along the fine-tuning displacement. These plots are not paired with measured training–test error gaps or comparisons of generalization-measure rankings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FSAM yields flatter visualized loss landscapes than Adam and SAM in the displayed RoBERTa-base fine-tuning settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The principal reported task scores are development metrics, not training-versus-test errors. Loss-landscape evidence is presented in figures without numerical sharpness comparisons. The authors state that they did not achieve actual sparse training or sparse speedup.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: the reported optimizer scores concern task performance and do not measure any claim version’s specified behavior or measure.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited or broader tuning, including the stated recovery strategies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that reduce those effects.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance tracking training–test error gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's gate rationale: V4 does not require a training–test gap measurement; held-out performance can suffice. The decisive mismatch here is the absence of adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons. Likewise, filter normalization makes the landscape evidence scale-aware, but does not establish V7's specified perturbation-tolerance versus generalization-gap relationship. No qualifying result rows need adding.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization.
Width sweep past interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures trained from scratch.
Adaptive optimizer comparison in the version's limited-tuning setting and its held-out versus training-performance gap.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
